evals.name: tr-kupon-uctan-uca
evals.prompt: Ekteki kupon user story'si (evals/files/kupon-user-story.md) için baştan sona test analizi yap: gereksinimleri analiz et, test case'leri çıkar ve Xray'e import edebileceğim CSV'yi hazırla. Sorulara cevap bekleme, makul varsayımlarla ilerle ama varsayımları belirt.
evals.expected_output: Turkish QA package: normalized requirements with IDs, flagged issues (vague 'hızlı', TBD guest rule, open-ended 'vb.'), clarification questions, boundary tests at 100 TL and at the 500 TL cap point, negative tests (expired, reuse), traceability, and an Xray CSV with step rows.

assertions.text: Requirements are normalized into a structured list/file where each has a stable ID (e.g. REQ-001) and at least 6 requirements exist
The analysis flags AC-5 'hızlı' as unmeasurable/vague and proposes a measurable threshold or asks a question
The analysis flags the guest-user rule (AC-6, 'belirlenecek') as unresolved/contradicting the registered-customer story and raises it as a question
A clarification question list exists with at least 5 questions, and questions include options or a default assumption
Test cases include boundary values around the 100 TL threshold (both 100,00 and a value just below such as 99,99)
Test cases cover the 50 TL maximum-discount cap including the point where 10% equals 50 TL (a 500 TL basket) and a value above it
There is a negative test for using the same coupon a second time by the same user
Every test case references at least one requirement ID
An Xray-importable CSV file exists with a test identifier column plus step columns (Action / Data / Expected Result) and multi-step tests span multiple rows under the same test id
Human-readable artifacts (test titles, steps, questions) are written in Turkish
Priorities are calibrated: at most 20% of test cases are critical and critical+high together are at most 60% (count programmatically)
The suite is proportionate for a 6-AC story: between 15 and 45 test cases
Derived/inferred requirements are limited (at most 8) and each is explicitly marked as unconfirmed

evals.name: en-loan-requirements-review
evals.prompt: We're about to start testing the loan application feature. Please review the requirements in evals/files/loan-srs.md for quality and testability before we write any tests. I need a list of the problems and the questions I should send to the product owner.
evals.expected_output: English requirements review: TBD (FR-7), age contradiction FR-1 vs FR-4, vague/compound FR-5 with 'etc.', unmeasurable NFR-1, missing upper bound / inclusivity for score, undefined withdraw target state and missing transitions, plus a prioritized question list with options/defaults; missing NFRs (performance, accessibility, privacy).

assertions.text: FR-7 is flagged as incomplete because of 'TBD'
The overlap/contradiction between FR-1 (18-65) and FR-4 (over 21 online, others at branch) is identified
FR-5 is flagged both as vague ('quickly') and as compound/open-ended ('etc.' or multiple obligations)
NFR-1 is flagged as unmeasurable ('secure', 'highly available') with a proposal for measurable criteria
Boundary ambiguity is raised: inclusivity of ranges (e.g. 'between 18 and 65', 'between 1,000 and 50,000') and/or the missing upper limit of the credit score
FR-6 is analysed as a state model: the target state of 'withdrawn' and/or other undefined transitions (e.g. withdraw from In Review, re-submission after Rejected) are raised
Missing requirement areas are identified beyond the text (at least two of: performance thresholds, accessibility, data privacy/KVKK/GDPR, audit, error handling, roles/permissions)
A prioritized question list for the product owner exists with at least 7 questions, each tied to a requirement ID
Every question sent to the product owner offers concrete options or a default assumption (not just an open question)
The conflict between FR-3 automatic approve/reject and FR-6's mandatory 'In Review' step is identified

evals.name: tr-odeme-tasarim
evals.prompt: evals/files/odeme-kurallari.md dosyasındaki ödeme ekranı için test tasarımı yap. Taksit kurallarını karar tablosuyla, ortam uyumluluğunu kombinasyon (pairwise) tekniğiyle ele al. Test case'leri ve gereksinim-test kapsam matrisini ver.
evals.expected_output: Turkish test design: decision table over card type / basket ≥500 / campaign / foreign card with gaps (e.g. wallet installments, 500 inclusivity) surfaced; boundary tests at 500 TL; pairwise set covering all valid pairs while respecting Safari/Edge constraints with far fewer than 96 rows; test cases linked to R1-R5; coverage matrix.

assertions.text: A decision table is produced whose conditions include card type, basket amount ≥ 500 TL, campaign product presence and domestic/foreign card
At least one rule gap or ambiguity is surfaced as a question (e.g. installments for digital wallet, foreign debit card, whether exactly 500 TL counts, what 'taksit seçenekleri' shows under 500 TL)
Test cases include boundary values at the 500 TL threshold (500,00 and 499,99)
The pairwise combination table contains no Safari+Windows/Android rows and no Edge+iOS/Android rows
The pairwise table covers every valid pair of browser/OS/payment/language values (verified) with fewer than 30 rows
Every test case is linked to at least one requirement (R1-R5 or REQ IDs)
A requirement-to-test coverage matrix is provided showing every requirement R1-R5 with its tests
Test cases and matrix are written in Turkish
The R1/R4 conflict (foreign credit card with basket >= 500 TL: R1 shows installments, R4 forbids them) is explicitly surfaced as a conflict or question, not silently resolved
Priorities are calibrated: at most 20% of test cases are critical and critical+high together are at most 60% (count programmatically; for runs without explicit priorities, FAIL)
